-- Group-kernel-normal-subgroup.agda
--
-- File: data/benchmarks/agda-algebras-hard-v0/obligations/Group-kernel-normal-subgroup.agda
--
-- Benchmark obligation: hard-group-kernel-normal-subgroup
-- Difficulty: non-obvious
-- Import stratum: novel
--
-- The kernel of a group homomorphism, as the predicate { x ∣ h x ≈ ε }, is a normal subgroup, and its coset relation is the kernel congruence: x ⁻¹ ∙ y lies in the kernel exactly when h x ≈ h y.
--
module Group-kernel-normal-subgroup where

open import AgdaDojang.Debug

open import Data.Product                  using ( _,_ ; _×_ ; Σ-syntax ; proj₁ ; proj₂ )
open import Level                         using ( Level ; _⊔_ )
open import Relation.Binary               using ( Setoid )
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions   using ( _Respects_ )
open import Relation.Unary                using ( Pred ; _∈_ ; _⊆_ )

open import Classical.Structures.Group.Basic         using ( Group ; module Group-Op )
open import Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups     using ( IsSubgroup )
open import Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation   using ( module Conjugate )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic                    using ( 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] )
open import Function.Bundles              using () renaming ( Func to _⟶_ )
open import Setoid.Homomorphisms.Basic               using ( hom )

module _ {α ρ β ρᵇ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) (𝓗 : Group β ρᵇ)
  ((hmap , hhom) : hom (proj₁ 𝒢) (proj₁ 𝓗))
  where
  private
    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    h = _⟶_.to hmap
  open Setoid 𝔻[ proj₁ 𝓗 ] using () renaming ( _≈_ to _≈ᴴ_ )
  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; _⁻¹ )
  open Group-Op 𝓗 using () renaming ( ε to εᴴ )

  Ker : Pred G ρᵇ
  Ker x = h x ≈ᴴ εᴴ

  kernel-normal-subgroup
    :  IsSubgroup 𝒢 Ker × Conjugate.IsNormal 𝒢 Ker
    ×  (∀ x y → ((x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∈ Ker → h x ≈ᴴ h y) × (h x ≈ᴴ h y → (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∈ Ker))
  kernel-normal-subgroup = {!!}

1	---
2	layout: default
3	file: "src/Classical/Structures/Group/Basic.lagda.md"
4	title: "Classical.Structures.Group.Basic module"
5	date: "2026-07-12"
6	author: "the agda-algebras development team"
7	---
8	
9	### Groups {#classical-structures-group}
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	A **group** is an inhabitant of the `Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ Th-Group` type,
14	where `Algebra` is parameterized by the signature type `Sig-Group`.
15	
16	The signature of `Group` grows over its predecessor's by a *unary* symbol
17	(`Sig-Group` adds `⁻¹-Op` to `Sig-Monoid`); its forgetful projection
18	`group→monoid` is therefore a reduct that drops `⁻¹-Op`, discharging the three
19	monoid equations on the reduct by the curried-law pivot of the `monoid→semigroup`
20	of [`Classical.Structures.Monoid`][Classical.Structures.Monoid] (here extended
21	from one law to three, the two identity laws additionally bridging the nullary
22	`ε-Op` node).
23	
24	This module follows the [Monoid][Classical.Structures.Monoid] template, adding the
25	following to it.
26	
27	+  **Direct curried accessors for all three operations**.
28	   `Group-Op` defines `_∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑨)`, `ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑨)`, and
29	   `_⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨)` directly over `Sig-Group`, never inheriting through
30	   the reduct, for the same reason Monoid gives: keeping the accessors direct
31	   keeps every downstream `refl` off the reduct's position-map reduction.
32	
33	+  **A unary node-bridge**.  Alongside the binary `interp-node-∙` and nullary
34	   `interp-node-ε`, `Group-Op` has `interp-node-⁻¹` for the unary `⁻¹-Op`, a
35	   one-liner delegating to `interp-cong` exactly as the other two do.
36	
37	+  **Two inverse laws**.  `invˡ-law` and `invʳ-law` join the three monoid laws in
38	   `Group-Op`; they are the only laws not consumed by the forgetful projection
39	   (which lands in `Monoid`, below the inverse structure), so they live in
40	   `Group-Op` rather than in the standalone curried-law block.
41	
42	<!--
43	```agda
44	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
45	
46	module Classical.Structures.Group.Basic where
47	
48	open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )
49	
50	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library -------------------------------------------------------
51	open import Data.Fin.Base                          using ( Fin )
52	open import Data.Fin.Patterns                      using ( 0F ; 1F ; 2F )
53	open import Data.Product                           using ( Σ-syntax ; _×_ ; _,_ ; proj₁ ; proj₂ )
54	open import Function                               using ( Func ; id )
55	open import Level                                  using ( Level ; _⊔_ ; suc )
56	open import Relation.Binary                        using ( Setoid )
57	open import Relation.Binary.PropositionalEquality  using ( _≡_ ; refl ; cong ; cong₂ ; setoid )
58	
59	import Relation.Binary.Reasoning.Setoid as SetoidReasoning
60	
61	open Func renaming ( to to _⟨$⟩_ ; cong to ≈cong )
62	
63	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library -----------------------------------------------
64	open import Classical.Operations              using  ( pair ; Curry₂ ; Curry₁ ; Curry₀ )
65	open import Classical.Signatures.Monoid       using  ( Sig-Monoid ; Op-Monoid )
66	                                              renaming ( ∙-Op to ∙-Opᵐᵒ ; ε-Op to ε-Opᵐᵒ )
67	open import Classical.Signatures.Group        using  ( Sig-Group ; Op-Group ; ∙-Op
68	                                                     ; ε-Op ; ⁻¹-Op ; ar-Group)
69	open import Classical.Structures.Interpret    using  ( interp-cong )
70	open import Setoid.Algebras.Reduct            using  ( reductBy )
71	open import Classical.Structures.Monoid       using  ( Monoid ; _⊨ᵐᵒ_ )
72	open import Classical.Theories.Group          using  ( Eq-Group ; Th-Group
73	                                                     ; assoc ; idˡ ; idʳ ; invˡ ; invʳ )
74	open import Classical.Theories.Monoid         using  ( Th-Monoid )
75	                                              renaming  ( assoc to assocᵐ
76	                                                        ; idˡ to idˡᵐ ; idʳ to idʳᵐ )
77	open import Overture.Operations               using  ( Op )
78	open import Overture.Terms                    using  ( Term ; ℊ ; node )
79	open import Overture.Signatures               using  ( ArityOf ; OperationSymbolsOf )
80	open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic             using  ( Algebra ; _^_ ; 𝔻[_] ; 𝕌[_] ; mkAlgebra )
81	open import Setoid.Terms                      using  ( module Environment )
82	
83	open import Setoid.Varieties.EquationalLogic  using  ( _⊧_≈_ )
84	
85	private variable α ρ : Level
86	```
87	-->
88	
89	#### The local satisfaction predicate
90	
91	```agda
92	infix 4 _⊨ᵍᵖ_
93	_⊨ᵍᵖ_ :  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ)
94	        (ℰ : Eq-Group → Term (Fin 3) × Term (Fin 3)) → Type (α ⊔ ρ)
95	𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ ℰ = ∀ i → 𝑨 ⊧ proj₁ (ℰ i) ≈ proj₂ (ℰ i)
96	```
97	
98	#### The type of groups
99	
100	`Group`{.AgdaFunction}` α ρ` pairs an algebra over `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} with a
101	proof of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction}.  Its own signature since the identity is a nullary
102	operation and the inverse is a unary one, and neither can be added to a weaker
103	signature by equations alone.  The five equations of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction} are
104	associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws.
105	
106	```agda
107	Group : (α ρ : Level) → Type (suc α ⊔ suc ρ)
108	Group α ρ = Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
109	```
110	
111	#### The reduct to monoids
112	
113	The container morphism `Sig-Monoid ⟹ Sig-Group` sends the monoid's `∙-Opᵐᵒ` and
114	`ε-Opᵐᵒ` to the group's `∙-Op` and `ε-Op`; the position maps are the identity.
115	`group→monoidAlg` is the induced reduct of the underlying algebra.
116	
117	```agda
118	mo-incl : Op-Monoid → Op-Group
119	mo-incl ∙-Opᵐᵒ = ∙-Op
120	mo-incl ε-Opᵐᵒ = ε-Op
121	
122	mo-κ : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Monoid)
123	  → ArityOf Sig-Group (mo-incl o) → ArityOf Sig-Monoid o
124	mo-κ ∙-Opᵐᵒ = id
125	mo-κ ε-Opᵐᵒ = id
126	
127	group→monoidAlg : Group α ρ → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} α ρ
128	group→monoidAlg 𝑮 = reductBy mo-incl mo-κ (𝑮 .proj₁)
129	```
130	
131	#### Curried associativity, standalone
132	
133	`gp-assoc` proves `x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)` for the group's own `∙`, a verbatim
134	port of `Monoid-Op.mn-assoc` to `Sig-Group`.  It is standalone, above the
135	forgetful projection, so both `Group-Op.assoc-law` and `group→monoid` consume one
136	proof.
137	
138	```agda
139	module _ ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
140	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl)
141	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
142	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
143	
144	  private
145	    infixl 7 _∙_
146	    _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
147	    _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
148	
149	    interp-node∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
150	      → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
151	    interp-node∙ s t η = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
152	
153	  gp-assoc : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
154	  gp-assoc x y z = begin
155	    x ∙ y ∙ z                ≈˘⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ ⟩
156	    ⟦ node ∙-Op lhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations assoc η ⟩
157	    ⟦ node ∙-Op rhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ' ⟩
158	    x ∙ (y ∙ z)              ∎
159	    where
160	    g0 g1 g2 : Term (Fin 3)
161	    g0 = ℊ 0F; g1 = ℊ 1F; g2 = ℊ 2F
162	
163	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
164	    η = λ { 0F → x ; 1F → y ; 2F → z }
165	
166	    lhs rhs : Fin 2 → Term (Fin 3)
167	    lhs = pair (node ∙-Op (pair g0 g1)) g2
168	    rhs = pair g0 (node ∙-Op (pair g1 g2))
169	
170	    γ : ∀ i → ⟦ lhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair (x ∙ y) z i
171	    γ = λ { 0F → interp-node∙ g0 g1 η; 1F → ≈refl }
172	
173	    γ' : ∀ i → ⟦ rhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair x (y ∙ z) i
174	    γ' = λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → interp-node∙ g1 g2 η }
175	```
176	
177	#### The `Group-Op` module
178	
179	`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}` 𝑮` is the named-accessor module for a fixed group, opened
180	at a use site so that the laws read in ordinary notation.  It rebuilds the
181	interface from `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} directly rather than inheriting it,
182	because the forgetful to monoids is a reduct along a signature morphism and so
183	carries nothing down.
184	
185	The three operations come first, curried out of their interpretations:
186	`_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε`{.AgdaFunction} and `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}.
187	`equations`{.AgdaFunction} is the satisfaction witness projected out of the Σ.
188	Then come the two congruences, `∙-cong`{.AgdaFunction} and
189	`⁻¹-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, and the three containment lemmas
190	`interp-node-∙`{.AgdaFunction}, `interp-node-ε`{.AgdaFunction} and
191	`interp-node-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}, one per operation symbol, each crossing the gap
192	between a law stated about interpreted terms and the same law in curried form.
193	
194	The five laws follow: `assoc-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `idˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction},
195	`idʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `invˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction} and `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.
196	Each is its `equations` step wrapped in the containment lemmas for the symbols it
197	mentions, so the inverse laws are the longest of the five: they mention all three
198	operations.
199	
200	```agda
201	module Group-Op {α ρ : Level} ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
202	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (trans to ≈trans; sym to ≈sym; refl to ≈refl)
203	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
204	  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
205	
206	  infixl 7 _∙_
207	  _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
208	  _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)
209	
210	  ε : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
211	  ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑮)
212	
213	  infix 8 _⁻¹
214	  _⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
215	  _⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑮)
216	
217	  ∙-cong : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x ∙ u ≈ y ∙ v
218	  ∙-cong x≈y u≈v = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → x≈y ; 1F → u≈v }
219	
220	  ⁻¹-cong : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹
221	  ⁻¹-cong x≈y = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → x≈y }
222	
223	  interp-node-∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
224	    → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
225	  interp-node-∙ s t = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
226	
227	  interp-node-ε : {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]} → ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
228	  interp-node-ε = interp-cong 𝑮 ε-Op (λ ())
229	
230	  interp-node-⁻¹ : (s : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
231	    → ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → s) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ⁻¹
232	  interp-node-⁻¹ s = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl }
233	
234	  assoc-law : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
235	  assoc-law = gp-assoc (𝑮 , equations)
236	
237	  idˡ-law : ∀ x → ε ∙ x ≈ x
238	  idˡ-law x = begin
239	    ε ∙ x                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong interp-node-ε ≈refl ⟩
240	    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0 ⟩
241	    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations idˡ η ⟩
242	    x                                                 ∎
243	    where
244	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
245	    η = λ _ → x
246	
247	    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
248	    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F
249	
250	  idʳ-law : ∀ x → x ∙ ε ≈ x
251	  idʳ-law x = begin
252	    x ∙ ε                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl interp-node-ε ⟩
253	    ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ g0 (node ε-Op (λ ())) ⟩
254	    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair g0 (node ε-Op (λ ()))) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations idʳ η ⟩
255	    x                                                 ∎
256	    where
257	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
258	    η = λ _ → x
259	
260	    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
261	    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F
262	
263	  invˡ-law : ∀ x → x ⁻¹ ∙ x ≈ ε
264	  invˡ-law x = begin
265	    x ⁻¹ ∙ x                                       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-⁻¹ g0 {η}) ≈refl ⟩
266	    ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op τ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η          ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ⁻¹-Op τ) g0 ⟩
267	    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair (node ⁻¹-Op τ) g0) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ equations invˡ η ⟩
268	    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η                     ≈⟨ interp-node-ε ⟩
269	    ε              ∎
270	    where
271	    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
272	    η = λ _ → x
273	
274	    τ : (_ : ar-Group ⁻¹-Op) → Term (Fin 3)
275	    τ = λ _ → ℊ 0F
276	
277	    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
278	    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F
279	
280	  invʳ-law : ∀ x → x ∙ x ⁻¹ ≈ ε
281	  invʳ-law x = ≈trans  (∙-cong ≈refl (≈sym (interp-node-⁻¹ (ℊ 0F) {λ _ → x})))
282	                       (≈trans  (≈sym (interp-node-∙ (ℊ 0F) (node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → ℊ 0F)) {λ _ → x}))
283	                                (≈trans (equations invʳ (λ _ → x)) (interp-node-ε {λ _ → x})))
284	```

286	#### The forgetful projection to monoids
287	
288	`group→monoid` takes a group to the monoid on its `(∙, ε)`-reduct: the underlying
289	algebra is `group→monoidAlg`, and the `Th-Monoid` satisfaction proof pivots
290	through `Group-Op`'s `assoc-law`, `idˡ-law`, `idʳ-law` by the curried-law-pivot
291	pattern of `monoid→semigroup`, the two identity laws additionally bridging the
292	nullary `ε-Op` node on the reduct.
293	
294	```agda
295	group→monoid : Group α ρ → Monoid α ρ
296	group→monoid 𝒢@(𝑮 , _) = 𝑹 , thm
297	  where
298	  𝑹 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} _ _
299	  𝑹 = group→monoidAlg 𝒢
300	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (refl to ≈refl)
301	  open Environment 𝑹 using ( ⟦_⟧ )    -- Sig-Monoid environment on 𝑹
302	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
303	  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; ∙-cong ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law )
304	
305	  -- 𝑹's binary node-bridge, over Sig-Monoid, landing in the group's curried ∙
306	  interp-node-∙ᴿ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
307	    → ⟦ node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
308	  interp-node-∙ᴿ s t η = interp-cong 𝑹 ∙-Opᵐᵒ λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
309	
310	  -- 𝑹's nullary node-bridge, landing in the group's curried ε
311	  interp-node-εᴿ : (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]) → ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
312	  interp-node-εᴿ η = interp-cong 𝑹 ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()
313	
314	  thm : 𝑹 ⊨ᵐᵒ Th-Monoid
315	  thm assocᵐ η = begin
316	    ⟦ Th-Monoid assocᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ xy (ℊ 2F) η ⟩
317	    ⟦ xy ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ z                   ≈⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) (ℊ 1F) η) ≈refl ⟩
318	    x ∙ y ∙ z                          ≈⟨ assoc-law x y z ⟩
319	    x ∙ (y ∙ z)                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 1F) (ℊ 2F) η) ⟩
320	    x ∙ ⟦ yz ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η                   ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) yz η ⟩
321	    ⟦ Th-Monoid assocᵐ .proj₂ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ∎
322	    where
323	    x y z : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
324	    x = η 0F ; y = η 1F ; z = η 2F
325	    xy yz : Term (Fin 3)
326	    xy = node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair (ℊ 0F) (ℊ 1F))
327	    yz = node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair (ℊ 1F) (ℊ 2F))
328	
329	  thm idˡᵐ η = begin
330	    ⟦ Th-Monoid idˡᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (node ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()) (ℊ 0F) η ⟩
331	    ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ _  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-εᴿ η) ≈refl ⟩
332	    ε ∙ _                             ≈⟨ idˡ-law _ ⟩
333	    _                                 ∎
334	
335	  thm idʳᵐ η = begin
336	    ⟦ Th-Monoid idʳᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) (node ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()) η ⟩
337	    _ ∙ ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (interp-node-εᴿ η) ⟩
338	    _ ∙ ε                             ≈⟨ idʳ-law _ ⟩
339	    _                                 ∎
340	```
341	
342	#### Group builders
343	
344	`opsToBareGroup` builds a raw `Sig-Group`-algebra from a carrier, a binary
345	operation, an identity element, and an inverse, over the propositional-equality
346	setoid `setoid A` — the empty-theory edge case of the `opsTo<family>` pattern, now
347	with one clause per `Sig-Group` symbol.
348	
349	```agda
350	open Algebra
351	
352	opsToBareGroup : {A : Type α}
353	  (_·_ : A → A → A) (e : A) (i : A → A) → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α α
354	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Domain = setoid _
355	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (∙-Op , args) = args 0F · args 1F
356	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (ε-Op , _) = e
357	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (⁻¹-Op , args) = i (args 0F)
358	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {∙-Op , _} {.∙-Op  , _} (refl , u≈v) = cong₂ _·_ (u≈v 0F) (u≈v 1F)
359	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {ε-Op , _} {.ε-Op  , _} (refl , _) = refl
360	opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {⁻¹-Op , _} {.⁻¹-Op , _} (refl , u≈v) = cong i (u≈v 0F)
361	```
362	
363	`eqsToGroup` builds a Group from the raw algebra plus the five equation proofs.
364	
365	```agda
366	eqsToGroup : {A : Type α} (_·_ : A → A → A) (e : A) (i : A → A)
367	  → (·-assoc : ∀ a b c → (a · b) · c ≡ a · (b · c))
368	  → (·-idˡ : ∀ a → e · a ≡ a) (·-idʳ : ∀ a → a · e ≡ a)
369	  → (·-invˡ : ∀ a → (i a) · a ≡ e) (·-invʳ : ∀ a → a · (i a) ≡ e)
370	  → Group α α
371	eqsToGroup _·_ e i ·-assoc ·-idˡ ·-idʳ ·-invˡ ·-invʳ = opsToBareGroup _·_ e i , proof
372	  where
373	  proof : opsToBareGroup _·_ e i ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
374	  proof assoc ρ = ·-assoc (ρ 0F) (ρ 1F) (ρ 2F)
375	  proof idˡ   ρ = ·-idˡ   (ρ 0F)
376	  proof idʳ   ρ = ·-idʳ   (ρ 0F)
377	  proof invˡ  ρ = ·-invˡ  (ρ 0F)
378	  proof invʳ  ρ = ·-invʳ  (ρ 0F)
379	```
380	
381	#### Setoid-level group builders
382	
383	`eqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} covers carriers with propositional equality.
384	
385	Group constructions in which the carrier is a bona fide setoid (e.g., the wreath
386	product of [Classical.Structures.Group.Wreath][], whose equality is
387	pointwise-and-pairwise) need a more general form, just as the lattice constructions
388	need `setoidEqsToLattice`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Lattice.Basic][].
389	
390	To address this need, `setoidOpsToBareGroup`{.AgdaFunction} assembles the
391	`Sig-Group` algebra from a carrier setoid, the three operations, and their
392	congruence proofs (which the propositional case got for free from `cong₂`{.AgdaFunction}).
393	
394	`setoidEqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} adds the five group equations, now stated over
395	the setoid equality `≈`.
396	
397	The interpretation clauses apply the argument tuple (`a 0F · a 1F` rather than
398	routing through `pair`{.AgdaFunction}), so each equation of `Th-Group` evaluates
399	definitionally to its curried form and the satisfaction proof consumes the curried
400	hypotheses directly; this is the same reduction discipline as in
401	`eqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} above.
402	
403	```agda
404	module _ (𝐷 : Setoid α ρ) where
405	  open Setoid 𝐷 using ( _≈_ ) renaming ( Carrier to D ; refl to ≈refl )
406	
407	  setoidOpsToBareGroup : (_·_ : D → D → D) (e : D) (i : D → D)
408	    → (∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x · u ≈ y · v)
409	    → (∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → i x ≈ i y)
410	    → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ
411	  setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong = mkAlgebra 𝐷 interp interp-congruence
412	    where
413	    interp : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Group) → Op (ArityOf Sig-Group o) D
414	    interp ∙-Op   a = a 0F · a 1F
415	    interp ε-Op   a = e
416	    interp ⁻¹-Op  a = i (a 0F)
417	
418	    interp-congruence : ∀ o {u v : ArityOf Sig-Group o → D}
419	      → (∀ j → u j ≈ v j) → interp o u ≈ interp o v
420	    interp-congruence ∙-Op   eq = ·-cong (eq 0F) (eq 1F)
421	    interp-congruence ε-Op   eq = ≈refl
422	    interp-congruence ⁻¹-Op  eq = i-cong (eq 0F)
423	
424	  setoidEqsToGroup : (_·_ : D → D → D) (e : D) (i : D → D)
425	    → (·-cong     : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x · u ≈ y · v)
426	    → (i-cong     : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → i x ≈ i y)
427	    → (·-assoc-≈  : ∀ a b c → (a · b) · c ≈ a · (b · c))
428	    → (·-idˡ-≈    : ∀ a → e · a ≈ a)
429	    → (·-idʳ-≈    : ∀ a → a · e ≈ a)
430	    → (·-invˡ-≈   : ∀ a → i a · a ≈ e)
431	    → (·-invʳ-≈   : ∀ a → a · i a ≈ e)
432	    → Group α ρ
433	  setoidEqsToGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong ·-assoc-≈ ·-idˡ-≈ ·-idʳ-≈ ·-invˡ-≈ ·-invʳ-≈ =
434	    setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong , proof
435	    where
436	    proof : setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
437	    proof assoc η = ·-assoc-≈  (η 0F) (η 1F) (η 2F)
438	    proof idˡ   η = ·-idˡ-≈    (η 0F)
439	    proof idʳ   η = ·-idʳ-≈    (η 0F)
440	    proof invˡ  η = ·-invˡ-≈   (η 0F)
441	    proof invʳ  η = ·-invʳ-≈   (η 0F)
442	```

### Groups {#classical-structures-group}

This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

A **group** is an inhabitant of the `Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ Th-Group` type,
where `Algebra` is parameterized by the signature type `Sig-Group`.

The signature of `Group` grows over its predecessor's by a *unary* symbol
(`Sig-Group` adds `⁻¹-Op` to `Sig-Monoid`); its forgetful projection
`group→monoid` is therefore a reduct that drops `⁻¹-Op`, discharging the three
monoid equations on the reduct by the curried-law pivot of the `monoid→semigroup`
of [`Classical.Structures.Monoid`][Classical.Structures.Monoid] (here extended
from one law to three, the two identity laws additionally bridging the nullary
`ε-Op` node).

This module follows the [Monoid][Classical.Structures.Monoid] template, adding the
following to it.

+  **Direct curried accessors for all three operations**.
   `Group-Op` defines `_∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑨)`, `ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑨)`, and
   `_⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨)` directly over `Sig-Group`, never inheriting through
   the reduct, for the same reason Monoid gives: keeping the accessors direct
   keeps every downstream `refl` off the reduct's position-map reduction.

+  **A unary node-bridge**.  Alongside the binary `interp-node-∙` and nullary
   `interp-node-ε`, `Group-Op` has `interp-node-⁻¹` for the unary `⁻¹-Op`, a
   one-liner delegating to `interp-cong` exactly as the other two do.

+  **Two inverse laws**.  `invˡ-law` and `invʳ-law` join the three monoid laws in
   `Group-Op`; they are the only laws not consumed by the forgetful projection
   (which lands in `Monoid`, below the inverse structure), so they live in
   `Group-Op` rather than in the standalone curried-law block.

#### The local satisfaction predicate

```agda
infix 4 _⊨ᵍᵖ_
_⊨ᵍᵖ_ :  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ)
        (ℰ : Eq-Group → Term (Fin 3) × Term (Fin 3)) → Type (α ⊔ ρ)
𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ ℰ = ∀ i → 𝑨 ⊧ proj₁ (ℰ i) ≈ proj₂ (ℰ i)
```

#### The type of groups

`Group`{.AgdaFunction}` α ρ` pairs an algebra over `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} with a
proof of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction}.  Its own signature since the identity is a nullary
operation and the inverse is a unary one, and neither can be added to a weaker
signature by equations alone.  The five equations of `Th-Group`{.AgdaFunction} are
associativity, the two unit laws and the two inverse laws.

```agda
Group : (α ρ : Level) → Type (suc α ⊔ suc ρ)
Group α ρ = Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra α ρ ] 𝑨 ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
```

#### The reduct to monoids

The container morphism `Sig-Monoid ⟹ Sig-Group` sends the monoid's `∙-Opᵐᵒ` and
`ε-Opᵐᵒ` to the group's `∙-Op` and `ε-Op`; the position maps are the identity.
`group→monoidAlg` is the induced reduct of the underlying algebra.

```agda
mo-incl : Op-Monoid → Op-Group
mo-incl ∙-Opᵐᵒ = ∙-Op
mo-incl ε-Opᵐᵒ = ε-Op

mo-κ : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Monoid)
  → ArityOf Sig-Group (mo-incl o) → ArityOf Sig-Monoid o
mo-κ ∙-Opᵐᵒ = id
mo-κ ε-Opᵐᵒ = id

group→monoidAlg : Group α ρ → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} α ρ
group→monoidAlg 𝑮 = reductBy mo-incl mo-κ (𝑮 .proj₁)
```

#### Curried associativity, standalone

`gp-assoc` proves `x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)` for the group's own `∙`, a verbatim
port of `Monoid-Op.mn-assoc` to `Sig-Group`.  It is standalone, above the
forgetful projection, so both `Group-Op.assoc-law` and `group→monoid` consume one
proof.

```agda
module _ ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (sym to ≈sym ; refl to ≈refl)
  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]

  private
    infixl 7 _∙_
    _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)

    interp-node∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
      → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
    interp-node∙ s t η = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }

  gp-assoc : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
  gp-assoc x y z = begin
    x ∙ y ∙ z                ≈˘⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ ⟩
    ⟦ node ∙-Op lhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations assoc η ⟩
    ⟦ node ∙-Op rhs ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op γ' ⟩
    x ∙ (y ∙ z)              ∎
    where
    g0 g1 g2 : Term (Fin 3)
    g0 = ℊ 0F; g1 = ℊ 1F; g2 = ℊ 2F

    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    η = λ { 0F → x ; 1F → y ; 2F → z }

    lhs rhs : Fin 2 → Term (Fin 3)
    lhs = pair (node ∙-Op (pair g0 g1)) g2
    rhs = pair g0 (node ∙-Op (pair g1 g2))

    γ : ∀ i → ⟦ lhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair (x ∙ y) z i
    γ = λ { 0F → interp-node∙ g0 g1 η; 1F → ≈refl }

    γ' : ∀ i → ⟦ rhs i ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ pair x (y ∙ z) i
    γ' = λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → interp-node∙ g1 g2 η }
```

#### The `Group-Op` module

`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}` 𝑮` is the named-accessor module for a fixed group, opened
at a use site so that the laws read in ordinary notation.  It rebuilds the
interface from `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction} directly rather than inheriting it,
because the forgetful to monoids is a reduct along a signature morphism and so
carries nothing down.

The three operations come first, curried out of their interpretations:
`_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε`{.AgdaFunction} and `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}.
`equations`{.AgdaFunction} is the satisfaction witness projected out of the Σ.
Then come the two congruences, `∙-cong`{.AgdaFunction} and
`⁻¹-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, and the three containment lemmas
`interp-node-∙`{.AgdaFunction}, `interp-node-ε`{.AgdaFunction} and
`interp-node-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}, one per operation symbol, each crossing the gap
between a law stated about interpreted terms and the same law in curried form.

The five laws follow: `assoc-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `idˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction},
`idʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}, `invˡ-law`{.AgdaFunction} and `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.
Each is its `equations` step wrapped in the containment lemmas for the symbols it
mentions, so the inverse laws are the longest of the five: they mention all three
operations.

```agda
module Group-Op {α ρ : Level} ((𝑮 , equations) : Group α ρ) where
  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (trans to ≈trans; sym to ≈sym; refl to ≈refl)
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
  open Environment 𝑮 using ( ⟦_⟧ )

  infixl 7 _∙_
  _∙_ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  _∙_ = Curry₂ (∙-Op ^ 𝑮)

  ε : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  ε = Curry₀ (ε-Op ^ 𝑮)

  infix 8 _⁻¹
  _⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  _⁻¹ = Curry₁ (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑮)

  ∙-cong : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x ∙ u ≈ y ∙ v
  ∙-cong x≈y u≈v = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → x≈y ; 1F → u≈v }

  ⁻¹-cong : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹
  ⁻¹-cong x≈y = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → x≈y }

  interp-node-∙ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
    → ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
  interp-node-∙ s t = interp-cong 𝑮 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }

  interp-node-ε : {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]} → ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
  interp-node-ε = interp-cong 𝑮 ε-Op (λ ())

  interp-node-⁻¹ : (s : Term (Fin 3)) {η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]}
    → ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → s) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ⁻¹
  interp-node-⁻¹ s = interp-cong 𝑮 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl }

  assoc-law : ∀ x y z → x ∙ y ∙ z ≈ x ∙ (y ∙ z)
  assoc-law = gp-assoc (𝑮 , equations)

  idˡ-law : ∀ x → ε ∙ x ≈ x
  idˡ-law x = begin
    ε ∙ x                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong interp-node-ε ≈refl ⟩
    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0 ⟩
    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair (node ε-Op (λ ())) g0) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations idˡ η ⟩
    x                                                 ∎
    where
    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    η = λ _ → x

    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F

  idʳ-law : ∀ x → x ∙ ε ≈ x
  idʳ-law x = begin
    x ∙ ε                                             ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl interp-node-ε ⟩
    ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η         ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ g0 (node ε-Op (λ ())) ⟩
    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair g0 (node ε-Op (λ ()))) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ equations idʳ η ⟩
    x                                                 ∎
    where
    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    η = λ _ → x

    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F

  invˡ-law : ∀ x → x ⁻¹ ∙ x ≈ ε
  invˡ-law x = begin
    x ⁻¹ ∙ x                                       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-⁻¹ g0 {η}) ≈refl ⟩
    ⟦ node ⁻¹-Op τ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ g0 ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η          ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ (node ⁻¹-Op τ) g0 ⟩
    ⟦ node ∙-Op (pair (node ⁻¹-Op τ) g0) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ equations invˡ η ⟩
    ⟦ node ε-Op (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η                     ≈⟨ interp-node-ε ⟩
    ε              ∎
    where
    η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    η = λ _ → x

    τ : (_ : ar-Group ⁻¹-Op) → Term (Fin 3)
    τ = λ _ → ℊ 0F

    g0 : Term (Fin 3)
    g0 = ℊ {X = Fin 3} 0F

  invʳ-law : ∀ x → x ∙ x ⁻¹ ≈ ε
  invʳ-law x = ≈trans  (∙-cong ≈refl (≈sym (interp-node-⁻¹ (ℊ 0F) {λ _ → x})))
                       (≈trans  (≈sym (interp-node-∙ (ℊ 0F) (node ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → ℊ 0F)) {λ _ → x}))
                                (≈trans (equations invʳ (λ _ → x)) (interp-node-ε {λ _ → x})))
```

#### The forgetful projection to monoids

`group→monoid` takes a group to the monoid on its `(∙, ε)`-reduct: the underlying
algebra is `group→monoidAlg`, and the `Th-Monoid` satisfaction proof pivots
through `Group-Op`'s `assoc-law`, `idˡ-law`, `idʳ-law` by the curried-law-pivot
pattern of `monoid→semigroup`, the two identity laws additionally bridging the
nullary `ε-Op` node on the reduct.

```agda
group→monoid : Group α ρ → Monoid α ρ
group→monoid 𝒢@(𝑮 , _) = 𝑹 , thm
  where
  𝑹 : Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Monoid} _ _
  𝑹 = group→monoidAlg 𝒢
  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ] using (_≈_) renaming (refl to ≈refl)
  open Environment 𝑹 using ( ⟦_⟧ )    -- Sig-Monoid environment on 𝑹
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; ∙-cong ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law )

  -- 𝑹's binary node-bridge, over Sig-Monoid, landing in the group's curried ∙
  interp-node-∙ᴿ : (s t : Term (Fin 3)) (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ])
    → ⟦ node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair s t) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ⟦ s ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ ⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η
  interp-node-∙ᴿ s t η = interp-cong 𝑹 ∙-Opᵐᵒ λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }

  -- 𝑹's nullary node-bridge, landing in the group's curried ε
  interp-node-εᴿ : (η : Fin 3 → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]) → ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ≈ ε
  interp-node-εᴿ η = interp-cong 𝑹 ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()

  thm : 𝑹 ⊨ᵐᵒ Th-Monoid
  thm assocᵐ η = begin
    ⟦ Th-Monoid assocᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ xy (ℊ 2F) η ⟩
    ⟦ xy ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ z                   ≈⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) (ℊ 1F) η) ≈refl ⟩
    x ∙ y ∙ z                          ≈⟨ assoc-law x y z ⟩
    x ∙ (y ∙ z)                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 1F) (ℊ 2F) η) ⟩
    x ∙ ⟦ yz ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η                   ≈˘⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) yz η ⟩
    ⟦ Th-Monoid assocᵐ .proj₂ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ∎
    where
    x y z : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
    x = η 0F ; y = η 1F ; z = η 2F
    xy yz : Term (Fin 3)
    xy = node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair (ℊ 0F) (ℊ 1F))
    yz = node ∙-Opᵐᵒ (pair (ℊ 1F) (ℊ 2F))

  thm idˡᵐ η = begin
    ⟦ Th-Monoid idˡᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (node ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()) (ℊ 0F) η ⟩
    ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η ∙ _  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (interp-node-εᴿ η) ≈refl ⟩
    ε ∙ _                             ≈⟨ idˡ-law _ ⟩
    _                                 ∎

  thm idʳᵐ η = begin
    ⟦ Th-Monoid idʳᵐ .proj₁ ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η   ≈⟨ interp-node-∙ᴿ (ℊ 0F) (node ε-Opᵐᵒ λ ()) η ⟩
    _ ∙ ⟦ node ε-Opᵐᵒ (λ ()) ⟧ ⟨$⟩ η  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (interp-node-εᴿ η) ⟩
    _ ∙ ε                             ≈⟨ idʳ-law _ ⟩
    _                                 ∎
```

#### Group builders

`opsToBareGroup` builds a raw `Sig-Group`-algebra from a carrier, a binary
operation, an identity element, and an inverse, over the propositional-equality
setoid `setoid A` — the empty-theory edge case of the `opsTo<family>` pattern, now
with one clause per `Sig-Group` symbol.

```agda
open Algebra

opsToBareGroup : {A : Type α}
  (_·_ : A → A → A) (e : A) (i : A → A) → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α α
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Domain = setoid _
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (∙-Op , args) = args 0F · args 1F
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (ε-Op , _) = e
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp ⟨$⟩ (⁻¹-Op , args) = i (args 0F)
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {∙-Op , _} {.∙-Op  , _} (refl , u≈v) = cong₂ _·_ (u≈v 0F) (u≈v 1F)
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {ε-Op , _} {.ε-Op  , _} (refl , _) = refl
opsToBareGroup _·_ e i .Interp .≈cong {⁻¹-Op , _} {.⁻¹-Op , _} (refl , u≈v) = cong i (u≈v 0F)
```

`eqsToGroup` builds a Group from the raw algebra plus the five equation proofs.

```agda
eqsToGroup : {A : Type α} (_·_ : A → A → A) (e : A) (i : A → A)
  → (·-assoc : ∀ a b c → (a · b) · c ≡ a · (b · c))
  → (·-idˡ : ∀ a → e · a ≡ a) (·-idʳ : ∀ a → a · e ≡ a)
  → (·-invˡ : ∀ a → (i a) · a ≡ e) (·-invʳ : ∀ a → a · (i a) ≡ e)
  → Group α α
eqsToGroup _·_ e i ·-assoc ·-idˡ ·-idʳ ·-invˡ ·-invʳ = opsToBareGroup _·_ e i , proof
  where
  proof : opsToBareGroup _·_ e i ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
  proof assoc ρ = ·-assoc (ρ 0F) (ρ 1F) (ρ 2F)
  proof idˡ   ρ = ·-idˡ   (ρ 0F)
  proof idʳ   ρ = ·-idʳ   (ρ 0F)
  proof invˡ  ρ = ·-invˡ  (ρ 0F)
  proof invʳ  ρ = ·-invʳ  (ρ 0F)
```

#### Setoid-level group builders

`eqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} covers carriers with propositional equality.

Group constructions in which the carrier is a bona fide setoid (e.g., the wreath
product of [Classical.Structures.Group.Wreath][], whose equality is
pointwise-and-pairwise) need a more general form, just as the lattice constructions
need `setoidEqsToLattice`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Lattice.Basic][].

To address this need, `setoidOpsToBareGroup`{.AgdaFunction} assembles the
`Sig-Group` algebra from a carrier setoid, the three operations, and their
congruence proofs (which the propositional case got for free from `cong₂`{.AgdaFunction}).

`setoidEqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} adds the five group equations, now stated over
the setoid equality `≈`.

The interpretation clauses apply the argument tuple (`a 0F · a 1F` rather than
routing through `pair`{.AgdaFunction}), so each equation of `Th-Group` evaluates
definitionally to its curried form and the satisfaction proof consumes the curried
hypotheses directly; this is the same reduction discipline as in
`eqsToGroup`{.AgdaFunction} above.

```agda
module _ (𝐷 : Setoid α ρ) where
  open Setoid 𝐷 using ( _≈_ ) renaming ( Carrier to D ; refl to ≈refl )

  setoidOpsToBareGroup : (_·_ : D → D → D) (e : D) (i : D → D)
    → (∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x · u ≈ y · v)
    → (∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → i x ≈ i y)
    → Algebra {𝑆 = Sig-Group} α ρ
  setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong = mkAlgebra 𝐷 interp interp-congruence
    where
    interp : (o : OperationSymbolsOf Sig-Group) → Op (ArityOf Sig-Group o) D
    interp ∙-Op   a = a 0F · a 1F
    interp ε-Op   a = e
    interp ⁻¹-Op  a = i (a 0F)

    interp-congruence : ∀ o {u v : ArityOf Sig-Group o → D}
      → (∀ j → u j ≈ v j) → interp o u ≈ interp o v
    interp-congruence ∙-Op   eq = ·-cong (eq 0F) (eq 1F)
    interp-congruence ε-Op   eq = ≈refl
    interp-congruence ⁻¹-Op  eq = i-cong (eq 0F)

  setoidEqsToGroup : (_·_ : D → D → D) (e : D) (i : D → D)
    → (·-cong     : ∀ {x y u v} → x ≈ y → u ≈ v → x · u ≈ y · v)
    → (i-cong     : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → i x ≈ i y)
    → (·-assoc-≈  : ∀ a b c → (a · b) · c ≈ a · (b · c))
    → (·-idˡ-≈    : ∀ a → e · a ≈ a)
    → (·-idʳ-≈    : ∀ a → a · e ≈ a)
    → (·-invˡ-≈   : ∀ a → i a · a ≈ e)
    → (·-invʳ-≈   : ∀ a → a · i a ≈ e)
    → Group α ρ
  setoidEqsToGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong ·-assoc-≈ ·-idˡ-≈ ·-idʳ-≈ ·-invˡ-≈ ·-invʳ-≈ =
    setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong , proof
    where
    proof : setoidOpsToBareGroup _·_ e i ·-cong i-cong ⊨ᵍᵖ Th-Group
    proof assoc η = ·-assoc-≈  (η 0F) (η 1F) (η 2F)
    proof idˡ   η = ·-idˡ-≈    (η 0F)
    proof idʳ   η = ·-idʳ-≈    (η 0F)
    proof invˡ  η = ·-invˡ-≈   (η 0F)
    proof invʳ  η = ·-invʳ-≈   (η 0F)
```

9	### Subgroups of an arbitrary group
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	For a group `𝑮`{.AgdaBound} presented as a Σ-typed structure over
14	[`Sig-Group`][Classical.Signatures.Group] (per [Classical.Structures.Group][]), a
15	**subgroup** is a subset of the carrier that is closed under the three basic
16	operations; that is, a *subuniverse* of the underlying algebra in the sense of
17	[Setoid.Subalgebras.Subuniverses][].
18	
19	This module generalizes the concrete treatment of the Klein four-group in
20	[Examples.Setoid.SubgroupLattice][] to an arbitrary group.
21	
22	Because the carrier of a setoid algebra comes with a setoid equality
23	`_≈_`{.AgdaFunction}, a subset that is to play the role of a subgroup in
24	theorems (conjugation, cosets, Dedekind's rule) must also be compatible with
25	that equality.  We therefore package a subgroup predicate as a record
26	`IsSubgroup`{.AgdaRecord} with two fields:
27	
28	+  `respects`{.AgdaField}: the predicate respects the setoid equality (`B Respects _≈_`);
29	+  `isSubuniverse`{.AgdaField}: the predicate is closed under the interpreted operations.
30	
31	The first field is invisible in the classical (`_≡_`-setoid) case, where it holds by
32	`subst`{.AgdaFunction}, and is exactly what setoid-based group theory needs.
33	
34	The second field alone already suffices to place the subgroup in the subuniverse
35	lattice of [Setoid.Subalgebras.CompleteLattice][] (see
36	[Classical.Structures.Group.SubgroupLattice][]).
37	
38	The module also provides the *curried closure toolkit*: a subuniverse of a group
39	algebra is closed under the curried `_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, contains `ε`{.AgdaFunction},
40	and is closed under `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}; and conversely those three closure properties
41	(together with `respects`{.AgdaField}) make a predicate a subgroup
42	(`mkIsSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction}).  The trivial subgroup `{ x ∣ x ≈ ε }` and the
43	full subgroup close the module.

79	#### Tuple-vs-curried interpretation bridges

81	The subuniverse machinery speaks of tuple-indexed operations `(f ^ 𝑨) a`, while
82	group theory speaks of the curried `x ∙ y`, `ε`, `x ⁻¹` of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}.

112	#### The curried closure toolkit

114	A subuniverse of the group algebra is closed under each curried operation.  These are
115	definitional consequences of closure under the tuple-indexed operations, because the
116	curried accessors of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule} are defined by applying the interpreted

---
layout: default
file: "src/Classical/Structures/Group/Subgroups.lagda.md"
title: "Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups module"
date: "2026-07-11"
author: "the agda-algebras development team"

### Subgroups of an arbitrary group

This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

For a group `𝑮`{.AgdaBound} presented as a Σ-typed structure over
[`Sig-Group`][Classical.Signatures.Group] (per [Classical.Structures.Group][]), a
**subgroup** is a subset of the carrier that is closed under the three basic
operations; that is, a *subuniverse* of the underlying algebra in the sense of
[Setoid.Subalgebras.Subuniverses][].

This module generalizes the concrete treatment of the Klein four-group in
[Examples.Setoid.SubgroupLattice][] to an arbitrary group.

Because the carrier of a setoid algebra comes with a setoid equality
`_≈_`{.AgdaFunction}, a subset that is to play the role of a subgroup in
theorems (conjugation, cosets, Dedekind's rule) must also be compatible with
that equality.  We therefore package a subgroup predicate as a record
`IsSubgroup`{.AgdaRecord} with two fields:

+  `respects`{.AgdaField}: the predicate respects the setoid equality (`B Respects _≈_`);
+  `isSubuniverse`{.AgdaField}: the predicate is closed under the interpreted operations.

The first field is invisible in the classical (`_≡_`-setoid) case, where it holds by
`subst`{.AgdaFunction}, and is exactly what setoid-based group theory needs.

The second field alone already suffices to place the subgroup in the subuniverse
lattice of [Setoid.Subalgebras.CompleteLattice][] (see
[Classical.Structures.Group.SubgroupLattice][]).

The module also provides the *curried closure toolkit*: a subuniverse of a group
algebra is closed under the curried `_∙_`{.AgdaFunction}, contains `ε`{.AgdaFunction},
and is closed under `_⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}; and conversely those three closure properties
(together with `respects`{.AgdaField}) make a predicate a subgroup
(`mkIsSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction}).  The trivial subgroup `{ x ∣ x ≈ ε }` and the
full subgroup close the module.

<!--
```agda
{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups where

open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )

-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------
open import Data.Fin.Base                 using ( Fin )
open import Data.Fin.Patterns             using ( 0F ; 1F )
open import Data.Product                  using ( _,_ ; Σ-syntax ; proj₁ )
open import Data.Unit.Base                using ( ⊤ ; tt )
open import Level                         using ( Level ; _⊔_ ; suc ; Lift ; lift )
open import Relation.Binary               using ( Setoid )
open import Relation.Binary.Definitions   using ( _Respects_ )
open import Relation.Nullary              using ( Dec )
open import Relation.Unary                using ( Pred ; _∈_ )

import Algebra.Properties.Group as GroupProperties

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------
open import Classical.Bundles.Group           using ( ⟨_⟩ᵍᵖ )
open import Classical.Operations              using ( pair )
open import Classical.Signatures.Group        using ( ∙-Op ; ε-Op ; ⁻¹-Op )
open import Classical.Structures.Group.Basic  using ( Group ; module Group-Op )
open import Classical.Structures.Interpret    using ( interp-cong )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic             using ( Algebra ; 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] ; _^_ )
open import Setoid.Subalgebras.Subuniverses   using ( Subuniverses )

private variable α ρ ℓ : Level
```
-->

#### Tuple-vs-curried interpretation bridges

The subuniverse machinery speaks of tuple-indexed operations `(f ^ 𝑨) a`, while
group theory speaks of the curried `x ∙ y`, `ε`, `x ⁻¹` of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}.
The two agree up to the setoid equality: `(f ^ 𝑨) a` applied to an arbitrary tuple
`a` equals the curried operation applied to the components of `a`, by congruence of
the interpretation (`interp-cong`{.AgdaFunction}).  These three bridges are the only
place the mismatch is handled; everything downstream uses them.

```agda
module _ (𝑮 : Group α ρ) where
  private
    𝑨 = proj₁ 𝑮
    A = 𝕌[ 𝑨 ]

  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]  using ( _≈_ )
                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
  open Group-Op 𝑮 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong ; idˡ-law )
  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ using ( ε⁻¹≈ε )

  -- The binary operation on an arbitrary 2-tuple is the curried ∙ of its components.
  interp-tuple-∙ : (a : Fin 2 → A) → (∙-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ a 0F ∙ a 1F
  interp-tuple-∙ a = interp-cong 𝑨 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }

  -- The nullary operation on an arbitrary 0-tuple is the identity element ε.
  interp-tuple-ε : (a : Fin 0 → A) → (ε-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ ε
  interp-tuple-ε a = interp-cong 𝑨 ε-Op λ ()

  -- The unary operation on an arbitrary 1-tuple is the curried ⁻¹ of its component.
  interp-tuple-⁻¹ : (a : Fin 1 → A) → (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ a 0F ⁻¹
  interp-tuple-⁻¹ a = interp-cong 𝑨 ⁻¹-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl }
```

#### The curried closure toolkit

A subuniverse of the group algebra is closed under each curried operation.  These are
definitional consequences of closure under the tuple-indexed operations, because the
curried accessors of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule} are defined by applying the interpreted
symbol to a canonical tuple.

```agda
  module _ (B : Pred A ℓ) (B-sub : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨) where
    -- A subuniverse is closed under the curried group multiplication.
    sub-∙-closed : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B
    sub-∙-closed {x} {y} x∈B y∈B = B-sub ∙-Op (pair x y) im
      where
      im : (i : Fin 2) → pair x y i ∈ B
      im 0F = x∈B
      im 1F = y∈B

    -- A subuniverse contains the identity element (the nullary operation forces it).
    sub-ε-closed : ε ∈ B
    sub-ε-closed = B-sub ε-Op (λ ()) (λ ())

    -- A subuniverse is closed under the curried inverse.
    sub-⁻¹-closed : ∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B
    sub-⁻¹-closed {x} x∈B = B-sub ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → x) (λ _ → x∈B)
```

#### The subgroup predicate

`IsSubgroup B` says the predicate `B` cuts out a subgroup: it respects the setoid
equality and is a subuniverse of the group algebra.  The record module re-exports the
curried closure properties, so `open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup` puts
`∙-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, `⁻¹-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, and
`respects`{.AgdaField} in scope for a fixed subgroup.

```agda
  record IsSubgroup (B : Pred A ℓ) : Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ) where
    field
      respects       : B Respects _≈_
      isSubuniverse  : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨

    ∙-closed : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B
    ∙-closed = sub-∙-closed B isSubuniverse

    ε-closed : ε ∈ B
    ε-closed = sub-ε-closed B isSubuniverse

    ⁻¹-closed : ∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B
    ⁻¹-closed = sub-⁻¹-closed B isSubuniverse
```

Conversely, an equality-respecting predicate that is closed under the three curried
operations is a subgroup: the tuple-indexed closure required by
`Subuniverses`{.AgdaFunction} follows from the curried closure by rewriting along the
interpretation bridges (this is the one direction that genuinely *uses*
`respects`{.AgdaField}).

```agda
  mkIsSubgroup : {B : Pred A ℓ}
    →  B Respects _≈_
    →  (∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B)
    →  ε ∈ B
    →  (∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B)
    →  IsSubgroup B
  mkIsSubgroup {B = B} resp ∙-c ε-c ⁻¹-c = record { respects = resp ; isSubuniverse = isSub }
    where
    isSub : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨
    isSub ∙-Op   a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ a)) (∙-c (im 0F) (im 1F))
    isSub ε-Op   a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε a)) ε-c
    isSub ⁻¹-Op  a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ a)) (⁻¹-c (im 0F))
```

#### The type of subgroups

A subgroup of `𝑮` at predicate level `ℓ` is a predicate on the carrier together with
a proof that it is a subgroup.

```agda
  Subgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
  Subgroup ℓ = Σ[ B ∈ Pred A ℓ ] IsSubgroup B
```

A **decidable subgroup** bundles a subgroup with a decision procedure for its
membership; this is the Layer-D presentation of a subgroup (ADR-008), mirroring how
`DecCon`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Finite.Basic][] bundles a
congruence with its decider.  Decidability is genuine data here: it cannot be
derived from carrier finiteness, since a predicate on a finite carrier need
not be decidable.

```agda
  DecSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
  DecSubgroup ℓ = Σ[ B ∈ Subgroup ℓ ] (∀ x → Dec (x ∈ proj₁ B))
```

#### The trivial and full subgroups

The trivial subgroup is the ≈-class of the identity, `{ x ∣ x ≈ ε }`; over a setoid
carrier the *class*, not the syntactic singleton, is the right notion.  The full
subgroup is the whole carrier.

```agda
  trivialSubgroup : Subgroup ρ
  trivialSubgroup = (λ x → x ≈ ε) , mkIsSubgroup resp ∙-c ε-c ⁻¹-c
    where
    resp : (λ x → x ≈ ε) Respects _≈_
    resp x≈y x≈ε = ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈ε

    ∙-c : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ ε → y ≈ ε → x ∙ y ≈ ε
    ∙-c x≈ε y≈ε = ≈trans (∙-cong x≈ε y≈ε) (idˡ-law ε)

    ε-c : ε ≈ ε
    ε-c = ≈refl

    ⁻¹-c : ∀ {x} → x ≈ ε → x ⁻¹ ≈ ε
    ⁻¹-c x≈ε = ≈trans (⁻¹-cong x≈ε) ε⁻¹≈ε

  fullSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Subgroup ℓ
  fullSubgroup ℓ =  (λ _ → Lift ℓ ⊤)
                 ,  mkIsSubgroup (λ _ _ → lift tt) (λ _ _ → lift tt) (lift tt) (λ _ → lift tt)
```

9	### Conjugation and normality
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	For a group `𝑮`{.AgdaBound} this module develops conjugation — first of elements
14	(`conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹`), then of subgroups — and the normality predicate, the
15	ingredients from which [Classical.Structures.Group.NormalCore][] builds the normal
16	core `Core_G(H)` as a complete-lattice meet.
17	
18	Two design points deserve comment.
19	
20	+  **The conjugate of a subgroup is defined as an image, not a preimage**.  We take
21	   `conjugate g B = { x ∣ ∃ h ∈ B , x ≈ conj g h }`, the ≈-saturated image of `B`
22	   under `conj g`, rather than the preimage `{ x ∣ conj (g ⁻¹) x ∈ B }`.  Over a
23	   setoid carrier the image form is superior: it respects the setoid equality *by
24	   construction* (no hypothesis on `B` needed), and it is a subuniverse whenever `B`
25	   is a bare subuniverse.  For equality-respecting `B` the two forms agree.
26	+  **Normality is the pointwise property** `∀ g x → x ∈ B → conj g x ∈ B`.  The
27	   bridge lemmas `normal-conjugate-⊆`{.AgdaFunction} and
28	   `normal-⊆-conjugate`{.AgdaFunction} recover the equivalent formulation "every
29	   conjugate of `B` coincides with `B`" when `B` respects the equality.
30	
31	All proofs are small equational chains over the group axioms; the derived
32	cancellation laws (`\\-leftDividesʳ` and friends) come from the standard library's
33	`Algebra.Properties.Group`{.AgdaModule} applied to the bundle view
34	`⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Bundles.Group][], which is what the bundle
35	bridge exists for.
36	
37	<!--

73	#### Conjugation of elements
74	
75	`Conj 𝑮` packages conjugation in the group `𝑮`; opening it puts `conj`{.AgdaFunction}
76	and its algebra of laws in scope.  The laws say: conjugation by a fixed `g` is a group
77	endomorphism (`conj-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-∙-hom`{.AgdaFunction},
78	`conj-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}), and as `g` varies it is a left action of the group on
79	itself (`conj-action-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-action-∙`{.AgdaFunction}) by
80	≈-automorphisms (`conj-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, with `conj-conj⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} and
81	`conj⁻¹-conj`{.AgdaFunction} the two inverse laws).

83	```agda
84	module Conjugate {α ρ : Level} (𝒢@(𝑮 , eqns) : Group α ρ) where
85	
86	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]  using ( _≈_ )
87	                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
88	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
89	  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
90	                        ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
91	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ
92	    using ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
93	
94	  -- Conjugation of the element x by the element g.
95	  conj : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
96	  conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹
97	
98	  infixl 30 conj-syntax
99	
100	  conj-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
101	  conj-syntax = conj
102	
103	  syntax conj-syntax g x = x ^ g
104	
105	  -- Conjugation is a congruence in the conjugated element ...
106	  conj-cong : ∀ g {x y} → x ≈ y → x ^ g ≈ y ^ g
107	  conj-cong g x≈y = ∙-cong (∙-cong ≈refl x≈y) ≈refl
108	
109	  -- ... and in the conjugating element.
110	  conj-congᵍ : ∀ {g h} x → g ≈ h → x ^ g ≈ x ^ h
111	  conj-congᵍ x g≈h = ∙-cong (∙-cong g≈h ≈refl) (⁻¹-cong g≈h)
112	
113	  -- Conjugation fixes the identity element.
114	  conj-ε : ∀ g → ε ^ g  ≈ ε
115	  conj-ε g = begin
116	    g ∙ ε ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idʳ-law g) ≈refl ⟩
117	    g ∙ g ⁻¹      ≈⟨ invʳ-law g ⟩
118	    ε             ∎
119	
120	  -- Conjugation by g is multiplicative.
121	  conj-∙-hom : ∀ g x y → (x ∙ y) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)
122	  conj-∙-hom g x y = begin
123	    (x ∙ y) ^ g                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g x y) ≈refl ⟩
124	    g ∙ x ∙ y ∙ g ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) y (g ⁻¹) ⟩
125	    g ∙ x ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g (y ∙ g ⁻¹)) ⟩
126	    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)))  ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (∙-cong ≈refl (assoc-law g y (g ⁻¹))) ⟩
127	    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (y ^ g))           ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) (y ^ g) ⟩
128	    (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)                  ∎
129	
130	  -- Conjugation by g commutes with inversion.
131	  conj-⁻¹ : ∀ g x → (x ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ⁻¹
132	  conj-⁻¹ g x = begin
133	    (x ⁻¹) ^ g              ≈⟨ assoc-law g (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
134	    g ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive g) (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ⟩
135	    (g ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ x) ⁻¹  ≈˘⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
136	    (x ^ g) ⁻¹ ∎
137	
138	  -- Varying the conjugator: conjugation is a left action of the group on itself.
139	  conj-action-∙ : ∀ g h x → x ^ (g ∙ h) ≈ (x ^ h) ^ g
140	  conj-action-∙ g h x = begin
141	    x ^ (g ∙ h)                ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
142	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (g ∙ h) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g h) ⟩
143	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
144	    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹    ≈⟨ ∙-cong (∙-cong (assoc-law g h x) ≈refl) ≈refl ⟩
145	    g ∙ (h ∙ x) ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g (h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
146	    g ∙ (h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹) ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
147	    (x ^ h) ^ g  ∎

### Conjugation and normality

This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

For a group `𝑮`{.AgdaBound} this module develops conjugation — first of elements
(`conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹`), then of subgroups — and the normality predicate, the
ingredients from which [Classical.Structures.Group.NormalCore][] builds the normal
core `Core_G(H)` as a complete-lattice meet.

Two design points deserve comment.

+  **The conjugate of a subgroup is defined as an image, not a preimage**.  We take
   `conjugate g B = { x ∣ ∃ h ∈ B , x ≈ conj g h }`, the ≈-saturated image of `B`
   under `conj g`, rather than the preimage `{ x ∣ conj (g ⁻¹) x ∈ B }`.  Over a
   setoid carrier the image form is superior: it respects the setoid equality *by
   construction* (no hypothesis on `B` needed), and it is a subuniverse whenever `B`
   is a bare subuniverse.  For equality-respecting `B` the two forms agree.
+  **Normality is the pointwise property** `∀ g x → x ∈ B → conj g x ∈ B`.  The
   bridge lemmas `normal-conjugate-⊆`{.AgdaFunction} and
   `normal-⊆-conjugate`{.AgdaFunction} recover the equivalent formulation "every
   conjugate of `B` coincides with `B`" when `B` respects the equality.

All proofs are small equational chains over the group axioms; the derived
cancellation laws (`\\-leftDividesʳ` and friends) come from the standard library's
`Algebra.Properties.Group`{.AgdaModule} applied to the bundle view
`⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Bundles.Group][], which is what the bundle
bridge exists for.

#### Conjugation of elements

`Conj 𝑮` packages conjugation in the group `𝑮`; opening it puts `conj`{.AgdaFunction}
and its algebra of laws in scope.  The laws say: conjugation by a fixed `g` is a group
endomorphism (`conj-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-∙-hom`{.AgdaFunction},
`conj-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction}), and as `g` varies it is a left action of the group on
itself (`conj-action-ε`{.AgdaFunction}, `conj-action-∙`{.AgdaFunction}) by
≈-automorphisms (`conj-cong`{.AgdaFunction}, with `conj-conj⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} and
`conj⁻¹-conj`{.AgdaFunction} the two inverse laws).

```agda
module Conjugate {α ρ : Level} (𝒢@(𝑮 , eqns) : Group α ρ) where

  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]  using ( _≈_ )
                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
  open Group-Op 𝒢 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
                        ; assoc-law ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ
    using ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )

  -- Conjugation of the element x by the element g.
  conj : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  conj g x = g ∙ x ∙ g ⁻¹

  infixl 30 conj-syntax

  conj-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
  conj-syntax = conj

  syntax conj-syntax g x = x ^ g

  -- Conjugation is a congruence in the conjugated element ...
  conj-cong : ∀ g {x y} → x ≈ y → x ^ g ≈ y ^ g
  conj-cong g x≈y = ∙-cong (∙-cong ≈refl x≈y) ≈refl

  -- ... and in the conjugating element.
  conj-congᵍ : ∀ {g h} x → g ≈ h → x ^ g ≈ x ^ h
  conj-congᵍ x g≈h = ∙-cong (∙-cong g≈h ≈refl) (⁻¹-cong g≈h)

  -- Conjugation fixes the identity element.
  conj-ε : ∀ g → ε ^ g  ≈ ε
  conj-ε g = begin
    g ∙ ε ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idʳ-law g) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ g ⁻¹      ≈⟨ invʳ-law g ⟩
    ε             ∎

  -- Conjugation by g is multiplicative.
  conj-∙-hom : ∀ g x y → (x ∙ y) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)
  conj-∙-hom g x y = begin
    (x ∙ y) ^ g                        ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g x y) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ y ∙ g ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) y (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g (y ∙ g ⁻¹)) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ (y ∙ g ⁻¹)))  ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (∙-cong ≈refl (assoc-law g y (g ⁻¹))) ⟩
    g ∙ x ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (y ^ g))           ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) (y ^ g) ⟩
    (x ^ g) ∙ (y ^ g)                  ∎

  -- Conjugation by g commutes with inversion.
  conj-⁻¹ : ∀ g x → (x ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ (x ^ g) ⁻¹
  conj-⁻¹ g x = begin
    (x ⁻¹) ^ g              ≈⟨ assoc-law g (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)       ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive g) (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ⟩
    (g ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ x) ⁻¹  ≈˘⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (g ∙ x) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    (x ^ g) ⁻¹ ∎

  -- Varying the conjugator: conjugation is a left action of the group on itself.
  conj-action-∙ : ∀ g h x → x ^ (g ∙ h) ≈ (x ^ h) ^ g
  conj-action-∙ g h x = begin
    x ^ (g ∙ h)                ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (g ∙ h) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g h) ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ (h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law (g ∙ h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) ⟩
    g ∙ h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹    ≈⟨ ∙-cong (∙-cong (assoc-law g h x) ≈refl) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ (h ∙ x) ∙ h ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law g (h ∙ x) (h ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
    g ∙ (h ∙ x ∙ h ⁻¹) ∙ g ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ≈refl ⟩
    (x ^ h) ^ g  ∎

  conj-action-ε : ∀ x → x ^ ε ≈ x
  conj-action-ε x = begin
    ε ∙ x ∙ ε ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (idˡ-law x) ε⁻¹≈ε ⟩
    x ∙ ε         ≈⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
    x             ∎

  -- Conjugating by g undoes conjugating by g ⁻¹, and vice versa.
  conj-conj⁻¹ : ∀ g x → x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g ≈ x
  conj-conj⁻¹ g x = begin
    x ^ (g ⁻¹) ^ g    ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ g (g ⁻¹) x ⟩
    x ^ (g ∙ g ⁻¹)    ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invʳ-law g) ⟩
    x ^ ε             ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
    x                 ∎

  conj⁻¹-conj : ∀ g x → x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹) ≈ x
  conj⁻¹-conj g x = begin
    x ^ g ^ (g ⁻¹)  ≈˘⟨ conj-action-∙ (g ⁻¹) g x ⟩
    x ^ (g ⁻¹ ∙ g)  ≈⟨ conj-congᵍ x (invˡ-law g) ⟩
    x ^ ε           ≈⟨ conj-action-ε x ⟩
    x               ∎
```

#### Conjugation of subgroups

The conjugate of a subset `B` by `g` is the ≈-saturated image of `B` under
`conj g`{.AgdaFunction}.  It respects the setoid equality by construction, and is a
subuniverse whenever `B` is (via the endomorphism laws above), so conjugation maps
subgroups to subgroups.

```agda
  -- The conjugate subset g B g⁻¹.
  conjugate : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  conjugate g B x = ∃[ h ] (h ∈ B × x ≈ h ^ g)

  infixl 30 conjugate-syntax

  conjugate-syntax : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  conjugate-syntax = conjugate

  syntax conjugate-syntax g B = [ B ]^ g

  -- The conjugate respects the setoid equality, with no hypothesis on B.
  conjugate-respects : ∀ g (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ) → [ B ]^ g Respects _≈_
  conjugate-respects g B x≈y (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , h∈B , ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈c

  -- Conjugation of an element lands in the conjugate of any subset containing it.
  mem-conjugate : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {x} → x ∈ B → x ^ g ∈ [ B ]^ g
  mem-conjugate g x∈B = _ , x∈B , ≈refl

  -- Conjugation of subsets is monotone.
  conjugate-mono : ∀ g {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ} {C : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ'} → B ⊆ C → [ B ]^ g ⊆ [ C ]^ g
  conjugate-mono g B⊆C (h , h∈B , x≈c) = h , B⊆C h∈B , x≈c

  -- The conjugate of a subuniverse is a subuniverse.
  conjugate-isSubuniverse : (g : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]) (B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ)
    →  B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮 → [ B ]^ g ∈ Subuniverses 𝑮
  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ∙-Op a im =
    h₀ ∙ h₁ , sub-∙-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h₀∈B h₁∈B , eq
    where
    h₀ h₁ : 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]

    h₁ = im 1F .proj₁

    h₀∈B : h₀ ∈ B
    h₀∈B = im 0F .proj₂ .proj₁

    h₁∈B : h₁ ∈ B
    h₁∈B = im 1F .proj₂ .proj₁

    eq : (∙-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g
    eq = begin

      a 0F ∙ a 1F       ≈⟨ ∙-cong (im 0F .proj₂ .proj₂) (im 1F .proj₂ .proj₂) ⟩
      h₀ ^ g ∙ h₁ ^ g   ≈˘⟨ conj-∙-hom g h₀ h₁ ⟩
      (h₀ ∙ h₁) ^ g     ∎

  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ε-Op a im = ε , sub-ε-closed 𝒢 B B-sub , eq
    where
    eq : (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a ≈ ε ^ g
    eq = begin
      (ε-Op ̂  𝑮) a  ≈⟨ interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 a ⟩
      ε             ≈˘⟨ conj-ε g ⟩
      ε ^ g         ∎

  conjugate-isSubuniverse g B B-sub ⁻¹-Op a im = h ⁻¹ , sub-⁻¹-closed 𝒢 B B-sub h∈B , eq
```

#### The normality predicate

A subset is **normal** when it is closed under conjugation by every group element.
The property is stated for bare predicates; for ≈-respecting subgroups it is
equivalent to each conjugate coinciding with the subgroup, and the three bridge
lemmas make both directions available in the form each client needs.

```agda
  -- The normality predicate: closure under conjugation, pointwise.
  IsNormal : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)

  -- For a respecting subset, normality bounds every conjugate above by B ...
  normal-conjugate-⊆ : {B : Pred 𝕌[ 𝑮 ] ℓ}
    →  B Respects _≈_ → IsNormal B → ∀ g → [ B ]^ g ⊆ B
  normal-conjugate-⊆ resp nrmB g (h , h∈B , x≈c) = resp (≈sym x≈c) (nrmB g h∈B)
```
